profile.address: Electron Avenue, Salem Township, Luzerne County, PA 18601
profile.reading: Nautilus Cryptomine, this registry's Building 2 of two mapped structures at the site, sits on Electron Avenue, Salem Township, Luzerne County, Pennsylvania 18601, co-located at Talen Energy's Susquehanna nuclear power plant. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press coverage and a Talen Energy SEC filing exhibit on Nautilus Cryptomine LLC, the facility is a joint venture between cryptomining and data center company TeraWulf and Cumulus Coin, drawing power directly from the co-located nuclear plant, a behind the meter power arrangement that has drawn broader industry and regulatory attention as large compute and cryptomining loads increasingly seek direct connections to nuclear generation for reliable, carbon free power. The site's total IT capacity is reported at 50 megawatts. TeraWulf is a publicly traded Bitcoin mining and, increasingly, AI and high performance computing infrastructure company that has positioned nuclear adjacent sites like this one as a differentiator for both low cost, reliable power and a lower carbon profile relative to fossil fuel powered mining operations. This registry's own OpenStreetMap sourced mapping shows two separate buildings at this site, numbered west to east; this row represents the easternmost, Building 2, while a companion row, Building 1, tracks the first structure. No square footage or facility specific certification detail was located for this specific building this session. This second building on the Nautilus Cryptomine campus shares its direct power connection to the 2.5GW Susquehanna nuclear power station, one of the largest nuclear plants in the United States, through the joint venture TeraWulf formed with plant owner Talen Energy in 2021. The arrangement was reported as among the first facilities in the country to source data center power directly from a nuclear plant behind the meter rather than through the regional grid. Talen purchased TeraWulfs minority stake in the joint venture in 2024, giving the power company full ownership of the physical campus while TeraWulf has continued to describe its operations there as unaffected by the ownership change.

reading.body:
Nautilus Cryptomine sits at Talen Energy's Susquehanna nuclear station in Luzerne County, Pennsylvania, and publishes 50 MW of IT capacity. At 40 kW per rack as a reference point for AI training density, this would equate to roughly 1,250 racks. The facility is co-located with nuclear generation, meaning power is available at site without grid dependency. The research status is exhausted, indicating no further public specifications are available.

Pennsylvania has mapped 14 data center facilities, but only four publish power consumption figures. Nautilus Cryptomine ranks fifth among published MW in the state, yet its 50 MW exceeds the total published capacity of the four disclosed facilities combined, which sum to 22.2 MW. This discrepancy reflects that most mapped facilities in Pennsylvania publish no figures. The operator's ownership was verified in September 2026.

No certifications, compliance designations, or AI-specific workload qualifications are published for this campus. The facility is documented as a joint venture between TeraWulf and Cumulus Coin, occupying two buildings in the registry. What workloads currently run there and what expansion plans exist are not in the published specifications.
